title: Your Life Expands as You Become More Yourself
author: Kathleen Schafer
source: Extraordinarily Ordinary: A Field Guide for Being Human (Substack)
summary: Schafer opens a May theme on expansion by arguing that real expansion — in leadership and in life — does not begin when circumstances get bigger but when a person becomes more fully themselves. The central enemy she names is the slow drift of 'ghosting yourself': abandoning your knowing to preserve belonging, muting what is true in order to remain comfortable in environments that cannot hold truth. Most people, she observes, do not do this all at once but through accumulated small compromises — adapting to systems that trade integrity for approval, truth for comfort, and contribution for compliance. The cure is what she calls the work of Authentic Self: choosing to stop negotiating with your own truth. She connects this to citizen leadership, arguing that honest leadership in the current moment specifically requires the capacity to speak truth with clarity — not blaming or demonizing, but the kind of truth-telling that opens conversations and creates movement toward the next best step. The piece uses spring as a metaphor for authentic expression: it does not ask permission to bloom.
points: The primary enemy of authentic leadership is not external opposition but the internal drift of 'ghosting yourself' — abandoning your own knowing through accumulated small compromises that slowly disconnect you from your center.

Systems that strip meaning from service — turning contribution into compliance, care into extraction, meaning into image — are the structural mechanism through which most people learn to become smaller than they are while calling it success.

The distinction between speaking truth and demonizing is critical: real leadership brings truth in a way that opens movement and reveals where agreement already lives, not in a way that strengthens division in the name of righteousness.

Expansion begins not with becoming better but with becoming less divided from what is already true — and the practical result is that choices get clearer, presence steadier, and relationships more honest.
Citizen leadership in the current moment requires people who trust themselves enough to stand inside the truth they see: you can only speak truth clearly if you trust who you are enough to say it.
quotes: Real expansion does not begin when our lives get bigger. It begins when we become more fully ourselves.

So much of what surrounds us pulls us away from ourselves. The pace of life, the pressure to perform, the confusion within our systems, the endless noise of reaction, all of it extends an invitation to abandon our center.
To ghost ourselves is to abandon our knowing in order to preserve belonging. It is to mute what is true in us so we can remain comfortable in environments that cannot hold truth.
Leadership begins the moment we decide to end that pattern.

Speaking truth is not blaming. It is not demonizing. It is not strengthening division in the name of righteousness. Real leadership brings truth in a way that opens movement. It reveals where agreement already lives, where cognitive dissonance is blocking progress, and where the next best step might be taken in genuine service to the whole.

When you are rooted in your nature, you are less easily moved by fear. When you trust your Gift, you are less likely to contort yourself for approval. When you know who you are, you are less willing to hand your voice to systems that depend on silence, distortion, or obedience.

The world does not need a perfected version of you. It needs your real presence. This is where expansion begins. Not in becoming better than you are. But in becoming less divided from what is already true.
